title: SPA/971/2018 of STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH SECRETARY URBAN DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT DEHRADUN Vs SURESH KUMAR

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 971 of 2018
With
Delay Condonation Application No. 18466 of 2018
State & another ...Appellants
Vs.
Suresh Kumar & others ...Respondents
Mr. Anil K. Bisht, Standing Counsel for the State-appellants.
Mr. Alok Mahra, Advocate for the respondent nos.1 to 15.
Mr. Gopal K. Verma, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Manav Sharma, Advocate
for the respondent no.16.
Dated: 15th December, 2018
Judgment
Coram: Hon'ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
 Hon'ble R.C. Khulbe, J.
Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J. (Oral)
 The delay of 87 days' in preferring the appeal is not
opposed and is, therefore, condoned. The application is disposed of.
2. This special appeal is preferred against the judgment
passed by the learned Single Judge in Writ Petition (S/S) No.3562 of
2017 dated 03.08.2018. The respondents herein filed the writ petition
to quash the order dated 04.10.2017 passed by the first respondent, to
declare the omission on the part of respondent no.1, in creating the
post of Safai Karmchari for Nagar Palika Bazpur, as unjust and
illegal; a writ of mandamus commanding the respondents to pay
minimum of the pay scales with allowances admissible for the post of
Safai Karmchari to the petitioners, as is being paid to other daily wage
employees of Nagar Palika Parishad Bazpur; a writ of mandamus
commanding respondent no.1 to create adequate number of posts for
regularization of eligible Safair Karmchari serving on contract in
Nagar Palika Bazpur; and a writ of mandamus commanding the
respondents to pass appropriate orders for regularization of the
petitioners in the post of Safai Karmchari from the due date with all
consequential benefits.

2
3. The respondents-writ petitioners had earlier filed Writ
Petition (S/S) No.744 of 2017, which was disposed of directing the
State Government to take a final decision in view of the
recommendation made by the third respondent to regularize the
services of the petitioners, after creation of equivalent posts, within a
period of ten weeks.
4. An order was passed by the first respondent on
04.10.2017 rejecting the claim of the petitioners on the ground that
they did not fulfill the condition of five years continuous service,
since they were on contract basis; and there was order of stay in Writ
Petition (S/S) No.154 of 2017.
5. In the order under appeal, the learned Single Judge
observed that it was not clear whether respondent no.1, while deciding
the representation filed by the petitioners, had considered the
subsequent letter addressed by the third respondent (Executive
Officer, Nagar Palika Parishad, Bazpur); it was the case of the
petitioners that employees, identical to that of the petitioners, working
in other Nagar Palika Parishads were regularized in service; mistake,
if any, was committed by the Nagar Palika Parishad, Bazpur;
subsequently another letter was sent by the third respondent for
correcting the mistake, which should have been considered; the first
respondent should have considered whether the petitioners' case was
identical to those whose services were regularized; and, if it was so,
the petitioners were entitled for the same treatment which was given
to the employees of other Nagar Palika Parishads. The order dated
04.10.2017 was quashed, and the first respondent was directed to take
a fresh decision regarding creation of post of Sweepers in the Nagar
Palika Parishad, Bazpur by considering the letter dated 18.06.2016
written by the third respondent. The learned Single Judge left it open
to the respondents to seek further information from the Nagar Palika
Parishad, Bazpur, and to consider the order passed in Writ Petition
(S/S) No.154 of 2017, if the same had any bearing on the present case.

3
A decision was directed to be taken within a period of two months
from the date of production of a certified copy of the order.
6. Sri Anil K. Bisht, learned Standing Counsel for the State-appellants, would submit that the petitioners' claim of parity with
employees of other Nagar Palika Parishads is wholly misconceived;
the petitioners are working only from 2010 and are not entitled for
regularization in terms of the Regularization Rules, 2013 (hereinafter
referred to the "2013 Rules") which provide for regularization of
persons employed on daily wages, work charged, contract, fixed
charge, part-time or ad hoc basis; the 2013 Rules provide that only
employees, who were appointed on daily wage basis prior to 2008, are
entitled to be considered; in any event, the validity of the 2013 Rules
is subjected to challenge in Writ Petition (S/B) No.616 of 2018, and
an interim order was passed by this Court directing the respondents
not to effect regularization in terms of the 2013 Rules; no mandamus
could have been issued to the authorities concerned to create posts;
and the order of the learned Single Judge, therefore, necessitates being
set-aside.
7. While Sri Alok Mahra, learned counsel for the
respondents-writ petitioner, would contend that the respondents-writ
petitioners have been working as contract workers ever since 2004, it
would not be appropriate for us to examine these factual disputes in
proceedings under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
8. Creation or abolition of posts is in the executive realm,
and no mandamus would, ordinarily, be issued by Courts directing the
executive to create or abolish posts, for these are all not matters for
the Courts to direct.
9. While the claim of the respondents-writ petitioners is, no
doubt, for regularization of their services, the question of
regularization would only arise after posts are created to
accommodate the petitioners herein. As the decision whether or not to

4
create posts is required to be taken by the Government, suffice it to
modify the order of the learned Single Judge, and instead direct the
respondent-Government to examine the various communications
received from the officials of the Nagar Palika Parishad, Bazpur; and
take a considered decision whether or not to create posts. The entire
exercise, culminating in a decision being taken either way (i.e.
whether or not to create additional posts), shall be completed at the
earliest, preferably within a period of three months from the date of
receipt of a copy of this order.
10. The present order is confined only to creation of posts.
Even if posts are created by the appellants, no further steps can,
evidently, be taken by them till Writ Petition (S/B) No.616 of 2018,
wherein the validity of the 2013 Rules is subjected to challenge on the
ground that it falls foul of the law declared by the Supreme Court in
Secretary, State of Karnataka and others vs. Uma Devi and
others, (2006) 4 SCC 1; State of Karnataka and others vs. M.L.
Kesari and others, (2010) SSC 247, is examined and considered by
this Court.
11. The appeal is disposed of accordingly. No costs.
 (R.C. Khulbe, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.)
15.12.2018 15.12.2018
NISHANT
